forms: tala tale tali talai talei tallu talla tal tel tele tile teli tare tlau trāyu
evidence: DEDR 3103 directly gives Tamil talai, Malayalam tala, Kannada tale, Tulu tare, Gondi tala/talla, Parji tel and Gadaba tallu ‘head’. The simple tal-/tel- survey forms agree in both stem and meaning; head-hair and head-fruit compounds are excluded.

forms: kan kannu kanni kanna kann kanu kane kanne kanny xann xan qanu kanul kannə kannɨ ken kenu kennu kon
evidence: DEDR 1159(a) gives Tamil kaṇ, Malayalam/Kannada kaṇ(ṇu), Gadaba kaṇ/kanu, Kurukh xann, Malto qanu and Brahui xan ‘eye’. These simple eye responses select subsection (a); the tears compounds in subsection (b) are excluded.

forms: muk mukku muku mugu mungu mungeli mungan mungan muŋan muŋgan muŋgel muŋgeli mukk
evidence: DEDR 5024 gives Tamil/Malayalam mūkku, Kannada mūgu, Tulu mūku/mūgu/mūṅku, Gadaba muŋan/muŋgan and Kui/Kuvi muŋgeli ‘nose’. These matching nasal/velar stems are distinguished from Gondi mosor and the unrelated survey responses.

forms: vay vai vayi vayu va bay bai bayi ba veyu vey poyi poi koy
evidence: DEDR 5352 gives Tamil vāy, Malayalam vāy/vā, Kannada/Tulu bāyi, Toda pōy, Konda veyu, Kurukh baī and Brahui bā ‘mouth’. Initial v-/b-/Toda p- is directly represented by the article; the distinct nōru and toḍḍi families are excluded.

forms: pal pall pallu palli palle pallu palu pel pellu pelli pannu paru
evidence: DEDR 3986(a) gives Tamil pal, Malayalam pallu, Parji pel, Gadaba pallū, Gondi pal, Kurukh pall, Malto palu and Telugu pannu ‘tooth’. The toothstick compounds of subsection (b) are excluded; source singular/plural elicitation labels are preserved.

forms: kai kay kayi kayyi kayu key kei keyi keyu ki kiy kiyu kiya kiyye ceyyi ceyi kaju kagu koy koi
evidence: DEDR 2023 gives Tamil kai, Kannada kay/kayi/key, Toda koy, Kolami kī/key, Gadaba ki/kiy, Konda kiyu and Telugu ceyi/ceyyi ‘hand, arm’. Only simple hand/arm forms are assigned; compounds for palm, elbow or particular sides remain separate.

forms: viral viralu veral veralu varal varalu virala vira virə bera beral beralu berulu berlu birel verl vende vande vanda reska
evidence: DEDR 5409 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam viral, Kannada beraḷ, Kodagu bera, Kota verl, Kolami vende, Parji/Gadaba vanda/vande and Konda ṛeska ‘finger’. The selected stems match these diagnostic lateral or -nd- series; aṅguli- and boṭṭa-type responses are separate families.

forms: ukir ugur uguru goru gor geri gere oy oyi
evidence: DEDR 561 gives Tamil/Malayalam ukir, Kannada/Tulu ugur(u), Telugu/Konda gōru, Parji gēri and Kodagu oy ‘nail/claw’. The article expressly corrects Kurukh oṛox to orox; rhotic-nail responses requiring that transcription judgment are held separately, as are Sanskrit nakha loans.

forms: kal kalu kel kelu kol kolu
evidence: DEDR 1479 gives Tamil kāl, Kannada/Telugu kālu, Kota kāl, Toda kōl, Parji kēl, Gadaba/Gondi/Konda kāl ‘leg, foot’. Exact elicited leg/foot senses are preserved; longer body-part compounds and Kurukh xeḍ are excluded.

forms: tol tolu toli togal togalu tokal tokalu toval tokka tolk tolka
evidence: DEDR 3559 explicitly groups Tamil/Malayalam tōl/toli/tokku, Kannada tōl/togal/toval, Telugu tōlu/tokka and Gondi tōl/tolka ‘skin, hide, rind’. These simple skin forms fit the printed family; carma-type Indo-Aryan loans are excluded.

forms: elumpu elumbu elambu elimbu ellu elugu elubu eluvu eluv elu elv elf yelugu yelubu yeluvu yemuka emuka emmu
evidence: DEDR 839 gives Tamil elumpu, Malayalam ellu/elumpu/eluṅku, Kannada elu/elubu/elugu, Kota elv and Telugu emuka ‘bone’. These forms are kept distinct from muḷe ‘marrow/bone’ and Indo-Aryan haḍḍa forms; the article's Sanskrit comparison is not asserted as ancestry.

forms: potta potte pota potti putti puta
evidence: DEDR 4494 explicitly lists Kannada poṭṭe, Telugu/Parji poṭṭa, Gondi poṭa/poṭṭa and Konda poṭa ‘belly/stomach’. It compares Prakrit poṭṭa without settling direction; the proposed Dravidian family placement retains that contact question and excludes unrelated vayir-/bairu forms.

forms: mulai mula mole mele mel mol
evidence: DEDR 4985 gives Tamil mulai, Malayalam mula, Kannada/Kodagu mole and Kota mel ‘breast’. The article specifically identifies Kota mol as borrowed from Badaga, so that exact Kota variant is held rather than treated as inherited.

forms: mel menu men meni mendul mendol mendur
evidence: DEDR 5099 lists Tamil/Malayalam mēl, Telugu/Kolami mēnu/mēn, Parji mēn, Gadaba mēnu and Gondi mēndul/mēndur ‘body’. These match the selected stems; mey belongs to the separately cross-referenced entry 5073, and oṭal/uṭampu forms require a different parent.

forms: kal kallu kalu kel kanda kandu xal
evidence: DEDR 1298 gives Tamil kal, Malayalam/Kannada kallu, Parji kel, Gadaba kanḍ(u), Gondi kal/kalli and Brahui xal ‘stone’. The matching forms are restricted by the stone sense, preventing confusion with kāl ‘leg’.

forms: ilai ila ele ela el elei ire
evidence: DEDR 497 gives Tamil ilai, Malayalam ila, Kannada ele/ela, Kota el and Tulu ele/ire ‘leaf’. Only this simple leaf stem is selected; the article's Gondi koṛk-ila ‘new leaf’ is a compound and is not reduced to a single inherited stem here.

forms: ver veru ber beru var voru vela
evidence: DEDR 5535 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam vēr, Kannada/Tulu bēr(u), Telugu vēru, Parji vār and Konda vēla ‘root’. The survey root senses and rhotic/lateral stems fit these comparanda; source forms are preserved without imposing one language's spelling on another.

forms: pukai puka poga pog poge puge pogo poya poyo poi bayi boyi boi
evidence: DEDR 4240 gives Tamil pukai, Malayalam puka, Kannada poge, Telugu poga, Gadaba pōgu, Gondi poya/poyo/poī and Kuvi bōyi ‘smoke’. The article itself documents the medial g/y variation; tobacco and longer verbal elicitation responses are outside this simple-noun selection.

forms: tingal tingalu tingol tingolu tigl tingl
evidence: DEDR 3213 gives Tamil/Malayalam tiṅkaḷ, Kannada tiṅgaḷ, Tulu tiṅgoḷu and Kota tigḷ ‘moon/month’. Source moon and month senses are retained; compounds for moonlight are excluded.

forms: nila nilavu nilaavu nela nelaci neling nelin nelenj nalenj lelenj lenj lenju lenzu
evidence: DEDR 3754 gives Tamil/Malayalam nilā/nilavu, Telugu/Kolami nela, Parji neliñ, Gadaba neliŋ and Gondi/Konda lēnj/lēnz ‘moon/month’. These forms belong to the nil-/nel-/lenj family rather than tiṅkaḷ or Indo-Aryan candra.

forms: maram mara marm mar mak maku maren marin maran meri meru man manu mann marnu mranu
evidence: DEDR 4711(a) gives Tamil/Malayalam maram, Kannada/Tulu mara, Kota marm, Kolami māk, Parji meri, Gadaba māren, Gondi mara and Kurukh mann ‘tree’. Only simple tree/wood responses are selected; the animal compounds in subsection (b) are excluded.

forms: udambu odambu udampu odampu udal odal odalu udalu orol
evidence: DEDR 586 explicitly gives Tamil uṭal/uṭampu, Malayalam uṭal/uṭampu, Kannada oḍal/oḍambi and Konda oṛol ‘body’. This is printed entry 586; the existing reconstruction at d585 has a mismatched body gloss and is deliberately not used.

forms: cevi cemi kevi kev keyv kivi kimi kemi kebi kavi kavu kevu kevvu kekol kekkol kekal gibi kibi xebda xaf kif
evidence: DEDR 1977(a) lists Tamil cevi, Alu Kurumba kevi, Kannada kivi/kimi/kemi, Gondi kevi/kavi, Parji/Gadaba kekol, Konda gibi, Kurukh xebdā and Brahui xaf ‘ear’. The separate Kui/Kuvi kri- subsection (b) is not folded into this analysis; deafness derivatives are excluded.

forms: ur uru uri
evidence: DEDR 752 gives Tamil/Malayalam ūr, Kannada ūr, Kodagu ūri, Tulu/Telugu ūru and Kolami ūr ‘village’. These simple village terms select the attested family; Brahui urā ‘house’ has a competing comparison in the article and is excluded.

forms: manai mana mane
evidence: DEDR 4776 gives Tamil maṉai, Malayalam mana, Kannada mane, Kodagu mane and Tulu mane ‘house’. The matching house responses preserve the simple stem; wife/household derivatives are not included.

forms: nay nai nayi ney netta nette nete ate noyi noy
evidence: DEDR 3650 gives Tamil nāy, Kannada nāyi, Toda nōy, Gondi nai/ney, Parji netta, Gadaba nette and Kolami āte ‘dog’. Its longer Konda nukuṛi analysis is qualified and morphologically complex, so that series remains outside this simple-form proposal.

forms: erumai eruma erima emme erme ermi armi hermi enumu
evidence: DEDR 816 records Tamil erumai, Malayalam eruma, Kannada/Kodagu emme, Tulu erme, Telugu enumu and Gondi ermi/hermi/armi ‘female buffalo’. Unqualified survey buffalo senses are compatible but do not identify sex; clearly male or compound responses are excluded.

forms: adu atu aru oda ode ude eti yeti eda ede het
evidence: DEDR 5152 gives Tamil/Malayalam āṭu ‘goat, sheep’, Kannada āḍu, Kota ār, Toda ōḍ, Gondi ēṭi, Kui ōḍa and Kurukh ēṛā ‘goat’. Source sex qualifiers remain visible; the printed Sanskrit comparison is not treated as a demonstrated donor relationship.

forms: panri pandi panni panji paji pajji paddi pend pendi pand pandu
evidence: DEDR 4039 gives Tamil paṉṟi, Malayalam panni, Kannada/Telugu pandi, Gondi paddi, Parji pend and Gadaba panḍu ‘pig’. These directly attested nasal-stop and nasal-affricate correspondences support the selected forms.

forms: min minu mini
evidence: DEDR 4885 gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada mīn, Parji mīni, Telugu/Kuvi mīnu and Gondi mīn ‘fish’. Simple min- responses are matched by both form and meaning; the article’s Sanskrit comparison does not itself establish borrowing direction.

forms: pampu pambu pappu pavu pamu pam pab pob bam bamu bambu
evidence: DEDR 4085 gives Tamil/Malayalam pāmpu, Kota pāb, Toda pōb, Kannada pāvu, Telugu pāmu and Parji/Gadaba bām ‘snake’. Tulu hāvu and Toda song ōf are explicitly loans in the article and are excluded from inherited-family proposals.

forms: pen penu peni pon
evidence: DEDR 4449 gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada pēn, Kodagu pēni, Telugu pēnu, Parji pēni and Kurukh nasalized pēn ‘louse’. The source’s flea compounds and Kui flea sense are distinguished; only louse responses are selected.

forms: irantu irandu randu rendu eradu erdu irdu indu indi indiŋ inding irat ira rend rand randi end endu irndu
evidence: DEDR 474 documents Tamil iraṇṭu/reṇṭu, Malayalam/Irula raṇḍu, Kannada eraḍu, Telugu reṇḍu, Gondi raṇḍ/reṇḍ, Parji irḍu and Brahui iraṭ ‘two’. Only the numeral two is selected; tens, distributives and multiword counted phrases are excluded.

forms: munru munu munnu mund mundu mundi munding muru mud mudu muduk mudug munji muji
evidence: DEDR 5052 gives Tamil mūṉṟu/mūṇu, Malayalam mūnnu, Kannada mūru, Telugu mūḍu, Gondi/Kurukh mūnd and Gadaba mūḍug ‘three’. The source directly documents these numeral-specific developments; thirty and longer distributive expressions are excluded.

forms: nal nalu nali nalku naku nangu nanku nalugu nalug naluŋ nalung naling nalgi nax naib
evidence: DEDR 3655 lists Tamil nāl/nālu/nāṉku, Malayalam nālu, Kannada nāku/nālku, Telugu nālugu, Gondi nāluŋ and Kurukh nāx ‘four’. These exact numeral responses are not confused with the day-word nāḷ.

forms: aintu aindu ancu ancu anju anji anj ayidu aydu aidu aid ayd endu eyndu eindu
evidence: DEDR 2826 gives Tamil aintu/añcu, Malayalam añcu, Kota anj, Kodagu añji and Kannada/Telugu ayidu ‘five’. The selected vowel-initial numeral forms fit that series; Indo-Aryan pañc forms are excluded.

forms: aru ar ari aji or ori
evidence: DEDR 2485 gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada āṟu, Kota ār, Toda ōṟ, Kodagu āri and Tulu āji ‘six’. The six gloss differentiates the numeral from similar river or interrogative forms; Indo-Aryan six responses are excluded.

forms: elu eru edu el eli ezu yezhu yezhu ezhu yelu yedu yeru
evidence: DEDR 910 gives Tamil/Malayalam ēẓu, Kannada ēẓu, Kodagu/Tulu ēḷi/ēḷu, Telugu ēḍu and Konda ēṛu ‘seven’. The numeral-specific lateral and retroflex series is explicitly documented; Indo-Aryan sāt forms are excluded.

forms: ettu et etu entu endu enimidi enamidi enumidi enumadi enumdi enmidi ettu yettu yettu
evidence: DEDR 784 gives Tamil/Malayalam eṭṭu, Kannada eṇṭu, Kota eṭ, Telugu enimidi and Kolami enumidi ‘eight’. The parent is printed entry 784, not d783, whose current reconstruction label misleadingly says eight over a different primary article.

forms: pattu pat patti padi padu patu pot hattu attu
evidence: DEDR 3918 lists Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada pattu, Kota pat, Toda pot, Kodagu patti and Telugu padi ‘ten’. Kannada hattu continues the familiar p-to-h correspondence; only ten responses are selected, with teen/tens compounds excluded.

forms: nuru nur nuri nudu
evidence: DEDR 3729 gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada nūṟu, Kota/Gondi nūr, Kodagu nūri and Tulu nūdu ‘hundred’. These single-word hundred responses select the documented family; explicit one-plus-hundred compounds are excluded.

forms: pal palu pali pel peru
evidence: DEDR 4096 gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada pāl, Telugu pālu, Parji pēl, Tulu pēru and Gondi pāl ‘milk’. The milk gloss distinguishes this family from pal ‘tooth’, even where survey length is unmarked.

forms: ney neyi neyyi neyyu neyyu nay ni niy niyi niyu
evidence: DEDR 3746 lists Tamil/Malayalam ney, Kota nay, Telugu neyyi, Gadaba neyyu and Gondi nī/ney ‘oil, ghee, fat’. Telugu nūne is explicitly a compound and is excluded from this simple-stem assignment, as are honey compounds.

forms: katti kati katte katy
evidence: DEDR 1204 gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada/Telugu katti and Tulu katte ‘knife’. Gondi is attested here only for a cock’s spur or attached fighting knife; general Gondi knife forms need a contact or sense judgment and are held.

forms: puli pulu pulla pulle pul puldi pullat huli
evidence: DEDR 4322 gives Tamil/Malayalam puḷi, Kannada puḷi/huḷi, Telugu pulla, Parji pul/puldi and Gondi pulla ‘sour’. The matching adjective stems select the acidity family; longer verbal inflections and tamarind compounds are excluded.

forms: mazai malai mara mala male mazhai mazha may maw
evidence: DEDR 4753 gives Tamil maẓai, Malayalam maẓa, Kannada maẓe, Kodagu/Tulu maḷe, Kota may and Toda maw ‘rain’. These simple stems are linked with the rain sense; rain-cloud or rainfall verbal compounds are excluded.

forms: na nakku nakk nakkɨ navu nav nava nalige nalage nalika naluka nalka nalke nalgu nalge nalayi nalay nalga nalangɛ nalange nalangu nalagu nalggu nalgi nalge nalukke naluga naliki nangu nang
evidence: DEDR 3633 gives Tamil/Malayalam nā/nākku/nāvu, Kannada nālige/nālage, Telugu/Konda nālika, Kolami nālka and Gadaba nāŋ ‘tongue’. These simple n-initial stems fit the documented series; Gondi vanjēr and Kurukh tatxa require different articles.

forms: nettur netturu nettar nettaru nettara netteru netur netir neter neteri netori nattur ditar
evidence: DEDR 3748 explicitly gives Kannada nettar, Telugu netturu, Gadaba nettūr/netir, Parji netir, Gondi nettur/nattur and Brahui ditar ‘blood’. This blood stem is kept separate from Kurukh xē̃s and from Indo-Aryan rakta-type responses.

forms: nir niru niri nilu nillu niru dir ir
evidence: DEDR 3690(a) gives Tamil/Malayalam nīr, Kannada nīru, Telugu nīru/nīḷḷu, Kolami īr, Parji/Gadaba nīr and Brahui dīr ‘water’. The water noun is distinct from the ashes article 3693; taṇṇīr and other compounds are excluded.

forms: ti tiy tu su
evidence: DEDR 3266 gives Tamil/Malayalam tī ‘fire’ and Tulu tū/sū ‘fire’. The short forms are admitted only with the fire gloss; longer burn verbs and heat derivatives are not collapsed into a fire noun.

forms: kiccu kicci kicce kis kic ciccu cicc cicu sisu hiccu hiccu tis tic tici
evidence: DEDR 1514 gives Tamil/Kannada kiccu, Kota tic, Telugu ciccu, Kolami/Gondi kis, Parji kic, Konda sisu and Kurukh cicc ‘fire’. Toda kic in songs is explicitly borrowed from Badaga and is excluded from inherited assignments.

forms: man mannu manu mann manna
evidence: DEDR 4666(a) gives Tamil maṇ, Malayalam/Kannada maṇṇu, Telugu mannu, Gadaba manu and Toda moṇ ‘earth, soil, mud’. Only the unextended earth/mud stem is selected here; maṇal ‘sand’ is separately distinguished in subsection (b).

forms: muttai mutta mutta motta motte mutte muty mot
evidence: DEDR 4939 gives Tamil muṭṭai, Malayalam muṭṭa/moṭṭa, Kannada/Tulu moṭṭe, Kodagu muṭṭe and Kota moṭ ‘egg’. These forms are distinct from guḍḍu and Gondi mēnj families.

forms: kompu kombu kommu komu kom kob
evidence: DEDR 2115 gives Tamil/Malayalam kompu, Kannada/Tulu kombu, Telugu/Gadaba kommu, Kota kob and Konda komu ‘horn’. Horn senses select this family; ordinary branch responses are not included in this proposal.

forms: uppu up uppi sup supp cup cuppu sor soru haru saru ovor havar
evidence: DEDR 2674(a) lists Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada uppu, Kolami sup and Parji cup ‘salt’; subsection (b) gives Gondi havar/ovor, Konda sōru and Kuvi hāru. The article supports the family but keeps the two stem series explicit; multiword salt responses are excluded.

forms: ulakkai ulakka olake onake onike alke olakke
evidence: DEDR 672 gives Tamil ulakkai, Malayalam ulakka, Kannada olake/onake/onike, Kodagu oḷake and Kurumba alke ‘pestle’. Printed entry 672 is used, not the incorrect pestle reconstruction associated with d572 (whose primary article is ‘ring’).

forms: ural uralu oral oralu orlu ora rolu
evidence: DEDR 651 gives Tamil/Malayalam ural, Kannada oral/oraḷ/orḷu, Kodagu ora and Telugu rōlu ‘mortar’. The source’s implement meaning is retained; this article is not used as a blanket parent for pestle responses.

forms: malai mala male mal
evidence: DEDR 4742 gives Tamil malai, Malayalam mala, Kannada male, Telugu mala and Toda mal ‘mountain, hill’. The questioned Gadaba mare comparison is excluded, as are longer forest compounds.

forms: campal campar sambal cambal sambalu sambaru
evidence: DEDR 2453 gives Tamil cāmpal/cāmpar and Malayalam cāmpal ‘ashes’. The proposal is confined to matching camp-/samp- responses; būdi forms have an explicit borrowing warning in DEDR 4316 and are not assigned as inherited here.

forms: nir niru nid id nivuru niguru
evidence: DEDR 3693 directly gives Tamil/Malayalam nīṟu, Telugu nivuṟu/niguṟu, Parji nīd and Gondi nīr ‘ashes’. The ash gloss differentiates these from nīr ‘water’ (3690); multiword ash compounds are excluded.

forms: mayir mayiru megaru meguru moyiru macir mir miru
evidence: DEDR 4707 gives Tamil/Malayalam mayir, Irula megaru/meguru/moyiru and Kota/Toda mīr ‘hair’. Only the bare hair noun is selected; tala-mayir ‘head-hair’ responses require an ordered component analysis.

forms: ondu vondu ondə ontu ontɨ oṇṇɛ onnɨ oṇrɨ oṇrī oṇṇu oṇṇɨ oṇḍɨ ɔndʰu ondy ondi onnu ɔntrɨ ɔntɨ onnə oru ōr ondru ontru onju onji vonji unḍu uṇḍī undi okkod okkōt ukkut ukkuṭ okuṭi okkuṭ okaṭi oṇṭā ort on ɔnd uṇ ond ōnd ōn ontā asiṭ asi asit ro obba
evidence: DEDR 990 explicitly groups the one numeral: (a) Tamil oru, Kannada obba, Kui ro, Kurux ort and Brahui asiṭ; (b) Telugu okaṭi, Kolami okkod and Gadaba ukuṭ; (c) Kurux oṇṭā; (d) Tamil oṉṟu/oṇṇu, Kannada ondu, Tulu oñji, Gondi undi and Kurux ōnd. The selected simple survey responses fit the corresponding branch; composite and divergent responses remain unassigned.

forms: ombadɨ vɔmbaṭṭu vombattu ombəttu vombadu ompatɨ onpatɨ ombatɨ ombadu ombaṭṭɨ omboḍu ombʰattu vambattɨ ombōdu vombaṭṭu vombāṭṭu ɔmbəttu oyimbady ɔrbat ombatu onbadɨ onbadu ombotɨ ɔmbotɨ ompōtu ompatu onpatu vormba unmā
evidence: DEDR 1025 gives Tamil oṉpatu/ompatu, Malayalam ompatu, Kannada ombattu/ombhattu, Kodagu oymbadi, Kota orbād, Tulu ormba and Gondi unmā nine. The retained variants preserve this numeral stem; Indo-Aryan nau/no and Telugu-type tommidi responses belong elsewhere.

forms: tommidi tomˑidi
evidence: DEDR 3532 explicitly lists Telugu tommidi and Gondi tomidi/tumīdī nine alongside Kolami tomdi. This proposal follows those attested languages; the similar Konda and Gadaba forms are excluded pending their inheritance versus Telugu-contact history.

forms: nalla nallatɨ nalladɨ nalladu nəllə nallə nɛllatɨ ṇalla
evidence: DEDR 3610 lists Tamil nal/nalla/nallatu and Malayalam nalla/nallatu good, Kodagu nalle and Kannada nalla. These survey stems and ordinary neuter inflections belong here; the stored parent label *nan-key is narrower than the primary article, which also covers the simple good adjective.

forms: periya perusu perəsə periyatɨ berī berīḍ ber berto bɛḍṭo bɛrṭo bɛrṭuṭ pedda perika berīa
evidence: DEDR 4411 connects Tamil periya/peritu, Telugu pedda, Gondi beriya, Konda per/peri, Parji berto and Gadaba berit big. These language-matched survey stems fit that family; the numerous valiya, doḍḍa and Indo-Aryan-looking alternatives are excluded.

forms: paḷaśɨ paḷasɨ paḷiya paḷaya paḷiyatɨ payadɨ paḷɛyatɨ paḷayatɨ paḷɛya paḷɛyɨ paLaya payadu paḍana padana patca pācʰā paṛayika
evidence: DEDR 3999 gives Tamil paẓa/paẓacu/paẓaiya, Malayalam paẓaya, Kannada paẓa, Gondi paḍana/paṛana, Konda paṛay and Kurux paccā old. The selected simple adjective forms follow these comparanda; old-person responses and compounds are kept out.

forms: taṇuppə taṇpu taṇṇige ṭannāge
evidence: DEDR 3045 records Malayalam taṇuppu coldness, Kannada taṇṇage/taṇṇane cool and taṇpu coldness. These responses continue the taṇ- stem; cold-water compounds and Indo-Aryan ṭhaṇḍo are not treated as simple inherited reflexes.

forms: sūṭu sūḍɨ cūḍɨ tsūḍɨ ṣūḍɨ śūḍɨ tsuḍɨ sūdu suḍu cūṭu
evidence: DEDR 2654 gives Tamil cuṭu/cūṭu burn/heat, Malayalam cūṭu, Kannada suḍu/sūḍu and Tulu cūḍu hot. The selected survey forms retain this stem with the palatal/sibilant and stop spelling variants; compounds and unrelated heat families remain outside this proposal.

forms: massor mosori mosor mosore mosar mossōr mūnji
evidence: DEDR 5031 attests Gondi massōr/mosor/mosoṛ nose and Kolami mūti mouth within the face/muzzle family. The differing survey senses are explicitly documented; questioned Toda nose/cheek comparisons are excluded. Konda mūnzi nose is also explicitly printed in this article.

forms: kukk kukka kukku kuk kūkk
evidence: DEDR 1630 directly compares Kurux kukk head or extremity with Malto kuku head. The Kurux survey head forms match the cited stem.

forms: balī bɛli bali
evidence: DEDR 5277 explicitly lists Kurux balī door or bamboo screen, Malto bali door screen, Parji vel doorway and Gadaba val door. The Kurux survey noun matches this family directly.

forms: tin tinu tinnu ṭīnnu ṭinu tinˑu
evidence: DEDR 3263(a) lists Tamil tiṉ, Kannada tin/tinu/tinnu and the widespread cognate eating verb; Kannada past stem tind- and related inflection belong here. Causatives, food derivatives and subsection (b) right-hand expressions are excluded.

forms: sā hā sāy sāyi sattu saṭṭu cā śā cay kah kahing kʰena kʰēnā kɛtcas kɛtcʰas kɛtcās
